text: A flood warning is in effect until 9:30 a.m. Wednesday for some of the hardest-hit parts of Brevard County. Standing water and multiple road closures are still making travel hazardous. Little more rain is expected, but even a small amount could cause problems where floodwater has not drained. Residents in flood-prone areas should stay cautious, avoid driving through standing water and check for road closures before heading out.

agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
text: Brevard Public Schools will reopen all campuses on Thursday, Nov. 5, after being closed three days because of the flooding. Buses, before- and after-school care, and after-school activities will run on their normal schedules. Bus routes in storm-affected areas may be delayed. Several Melbourne schools stay under a precautionary boil water notice through the end of the week.

agency: City of West Melbourne / Brevard County Emergency Management
text: The American Red Cross of North and Central Florida has opened a shelter for people affected by the flooding at Wickham Park Senior Center, 2785 Leisure Way, Melbourne, FL 32935. Never drive through flooded roads. Some streets in West Melbourne, Satellite Beach, Indian Harbour Beach and Indialantic are still blocked by standing water.
